claims.text: The synthesis route determines atomic ordering in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
The synthesis route determines phase homogeneity in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Atomic ordering governs the catalytic performance of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Phase homogeneity governs the catalytic performance of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Ball milling and chemical deposition produce different atomic diffusion kinetics.
Ball milling and chemical deposition produce different atomic mixing rates.
Compared with chemical deposition, high-energy ball milling promotes a more uniform atomic distribution.
Compared with chemical deposition, high-energy ball milling produces fewer defects.
A uniform atomic distribution and fewer defects provide a more favorable structure for catalytic active sites.
Ball-milled catalysts will form a more uniform solid solution than chemically deposited catalysts of the same precursor composition.
Ball-milled catalysts will have lower defect densities than chemically deposited catalysts of the same precursor composition.
Ball-milled catalysts will exhibit higher catalytic turnover frequencies than chemically deposited catalysts under identical test conditions.
Surface-site uniformity is critical in the oxidation or hydrogenation reactions covered by the proposed boundary.
XRD peak shifts and broadening can be used as indicators of solid-solution formation in the proposed materials.
